_comment: Generated by tests/fixtures/make_grouping_golden.py. Do not edit by hand. core/group.py and frontend/src/lib/group.js must both reproduce every case exactly, and their constants must equal the thresholds and grouping_version below. dc is compared to 1e-9.

cases.name: decision_table_rows
cases.description: One pair per table row and per threshold edge. MIN_GROUP=1 so the post-pass leaves the table's decisions untouched.

cases.name: fast_rule_or
cases.description: FAST_RULE=or: a quick follow-up splits on either strong signal.

cases.name: fast_rule_dh
cases.description: FAST_RULE=dh: a quick follow-up splits on structure alone.

cases.name: min_group_merges_into_nearer_neighbour
cases.description: 0004 is a singleton between two medium pauses. Distance to the previous group is 20 + 64*0.25 = 36, to the next 15 + 64*0.05 = 18.2, so it joins the next group. 0008 is a singleton with equal distances on both sides; the tie goes to the previous group.

cases.name: min_group_keeps_isolated_frames
cases.description: 0001 is a first frame followed by a hard gap: kept. 0004 has hard gaps on both sides: kept. 0007 is a last frame after a medium pause: merged into the previous group.

cases.name: max_group_split_respects_min_group
cases.description: Nine quick frames, MAX_GROUP=6. The largest distance is at the first pair, but cutting there would leave one photo, so it is not a candidate. The cut goes to the next largest (before 0007).

cases.name: max_group_split_tie_goes_to_middle
cases.description: Eight frames with identical distances, MAX_GROUP=6: the tie is broken toward the middle of the group, giving 4 + 4.

cases.name: max_group_split_repeats
cases.description: Fourteen identical-distance frames, MAX_GROUP=4: split in the middle (7 + 7), then each half again. A 7 can only be cut 4 + 3 or 3 + 4; both are equally near the middle, so the earlier cut wins (3 + 4).

cases.name: no_capture_times
cases.description: No photo has a capture time: filename order, visual_only rule (needs dh >= H_LOW and dc >= C_LOW).

cases.name: mixed_clocks_fall_back_to_filename_order
cases.description: 0003 and 0004 only have file mtimes, a day later than the EXIF times. Sorting by time would move them to the end. Order is by filename instead, and dt is used only where both photos share a clock: 0003-0004 (both mtime, 200 s apart -> time_gap) and 0005-0006 (both EXIF). Pairs across clocks use visual_only.

cases.name: missing_fingerprints
cases.description: 0003 has no fingerprint, so its pairs are decided on time alone (30 s: no boundary; 120 s: time_gap). 0006 has neither time nor fingerprint, so its pairs carry no data and never split. One missing EXIF time puts the shoot in filename order.

cases.name: capture_time_order_survives_counter_wrap
cases.description: Input arrives shuffled, and the DSC counter wraps from 09999 to 00001. Capture time is the primary key, so 09998 and 09999 stay ahead of 00002. 09999 and 00001 share a timestamp (1 s EXIF resolution); the filename breaks that tie, putting 00001 first.
